title: OpenID Connect
summary: OAuth says what an app may do; OpenID Connect says who signed in. id_token, nonce, userinfo, discovery, and how Entra ID, Auth0 and Keycloak fit.

steps.title: Authentication on top of OAuth
body: OAuth 2.0 gives a client an access token for an API. It does **not** tell the client who the user is: an access token is meant for the API, and its format is the API's business. Apps that "logged in with OAuth" by calling some profile API were tricked repeatedly.
**OpenID Connect (OIDC)** is a thin identity layer on top. Add the scope `openid` to the authorization code flow and the token response gains an **`id_token`**:
"id_token": "eyJ...",           // for the client: who signed in
The id_token is always a signed JWT, with claims such as:
- `aud` is the **client id**, not an API.
- `nonce` echoes a random value the client put in the `/authorize` request, which binds the token to *this* login and stops replays.
- Extra scopes `profile`, `email`, `address`, `phone` ask for standard claims. The **userinfo endpoint** (`GET /userinfo` with the access token) returns the same kind of claims on demand.
- Identify users by **`iss` + `sub`**, never by email: emails change and can be reassigned.

items: Contains a `nonce` from the login request
The client reads it to learn who signed in
Sent in `Authorization: Bearer` to an API
Its format is the API's business (may be opaque)

steps.title: Discovery
body: Every OIDC provider publishes its configuration at a fixed path under the issuer:

Libraries (including ASP.NET Core's `AddJwtBearer` and `AddOpenIdConnect`) need only the **authority** URL: they fetch this document, then the JWKS, cache both and refresh them periodically, which is how key rotation works without redeploys.

One rule: the `issuer` inside the document must **exactly equal** the issuer you expected, and must match the `iss` of the tokens. Otherwise a document fetched from the wrong place could point you at an attacker's keys.

steps.title: The providers you will meet
body: The protocol is the same everywhere; the names differ.
- Authority: `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant-id}/v2.0`. Apps are registered as **app registrations**; APIs "expose an API" with scopes like `api://orders-api/orders.read`.

- Access tokens put scopes in **`scp`** and app roles in **`roles`**. `oid` is the user's stable id across apps in the tenant, `tid` the tenant. Daemons use client credentials or, better, **managed identities**.

- Authority: `https://{your-tenant}.auth0.com/` (note the trailing slash in `iss`). Ask for an access token for your API by passing `audience=https://orders-api` to `/authorize`; without it you get an opaque token only good for userinfo. Custom claims must be namespaced URLs.
- Authority: `https://{host}/realms/{realm}`. A **realm** is a tenant. Roles appear as `realm_access.roles` and `resource_access.{client}.roles`.
Whichever you use, your API's job is identical: validate signature (via JWKS), `iss`, `aud`, `exp`, then authorize on scopes and roles.

steps.prompt: Match each provider to its issuer format.
A front-end sends its **id_token** as `Authorization: Bearer` to your API. The signature is valid and it isn't expired. What should the API do?
options: Reject it: its audience is the client id, not this API
Accept it, since it proves who the user is
Accept it only if it contains an email claim
Exchange it for an access token itself
steps.explain: An id_token tells the *client* who signed in. APIs must accept only access tokens whose `aud` is the API. Checking `aud` catches this mistake automatically.

steps.title: Validate id_token claims
prompt: The signature has already been checked. Write `string ValidateIdTokenClaims(string payloadJson, string issuer, string clientId, string nonce, long now)` that returns the first problem in this order:
3. `"bad_azp"`: `aud` is an array with **more than one** entry and the `azp` (authorized party) claim isn't `clientId`.
starter: string ValidateIdTokenClaims(string payloadJson, string issuer, string clientId, string nonce, long now)
solution: string ValidateIdTokenClaims(string payloadJson, string issuer, string clientId, string nonce, long now)
if (!root.TryGetProperty("iss", out var iss) || iss.GetString() != issuer) return "bad_issuer";
if (list.Count > 1 && (!root.TryGetProperty("azp", out var azp) || azp.GetString() != clientId)) return "bad_azp";
if (!root.TryGetProperty("exp", out var exp) || now >= exp.GetInt64()) return "expired";
if (!root.TryGetProperty("nonce", out var n) || n.GetString() != nonce) return "bad_nonce";
hints: Parse once with `JsonDocument.Parse`, then a chain of early returns.
For an array `aud`, collect the strings into a list; check `Contains(clientId)`, then `Count > 1` and `azp`.
template: string P(string aud, string extra = "") => "{\"iss\":\"https://login.example.com\",\"sub\":\"248289761001\",\"aud\":" + aud + ",\"exp\":2000,\"nonce\":\"n-0S6\"" + extra + "}";
Dojo.Eq("issued to another client", "bad_audience", ValidateIdTokenClaims(P("\"other-app\""), Iss, "my-app", "n-0S6", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("array aud with only us", "ok", ValidateIdTokenClaims(P("[\"my-app\"]"), Iss, "my-app", "n-0S6", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("array aud with two entries and no azp", "bad_azp", ValidateIdTokenClaims(P("[\"my-app\",\"api\"]"), Iss, "my-app", "n-0S6", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("array aud with two entries and azp = us", "ok", ValidateIdTokenClaims(P("[\"my-app\",\"api\"]", ",\"azp\":\"my-app\""), Iss, "my-app", "n-0S6", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("array aud with azp = someone else", "bad_azp", ValidateIdTokenClaims(P("[\"my-app\",\"api\"]", ",\"azp\":\"api\""), Iss, "my-app", "n-0S6", 1000));
Dojo.Eq("replayed from another login (nonce)", "bad_nonce", ValidateIdTokenClaims(P("\"my-app\""), Iss, "my-app", "n-OTHER", 1000));

steps.title: Read a discovery document
prompt: Write `(string Authorize, string Token, string Jwks)? ReadDiscovery(string json, string expectedIssuer)`:

- Return `null` when the JSON is invalid, `issuer` is missing or not exactly `expectedIssuer`, or any of `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `jwks_uri` is missing or doesn't start with `https://`.
starter: (string Authorize, string Token, string Jwks)? ReadDiscovery(string json, string expectedIssuer)
solution: (string Authorize, string Token, string Jwks)? ReadDiscovery(string json, string expectedIssuer)
root.TryGetProperty(name, out var v) && v.GetString() is string s && s.StartsWith("https://") ? s : null;
if (authorize is null || token is null || jwks is null) return null;
catch (Exception e) when (e is JsonException or KeyNotFoundException or InvalidOperationException)
hints: Wrap everything in `try` / `catch (Exception e) when (e is JsonException or KeyNotFoundException or InvalidOperationException)`.
A small local function `string? Https(string name)` keeps the three checks short.
template: Dojo.Eq("issuer differs by a trailing slash -> null", null, ReadDiscovery(Good, "https://id.example/"));
